overview.short: Bodh Gaya is the holiest Buddhist pilgrimage site on Earth, where Prince Siddhartha Gautama attained supreme enlightenment beneath the sacred Bodhi Tree in 534 BCE.
overview.description: Situated on the banks of the sacred Falgu (Neranjara) River in Gaya district, Bodh Gaya is the epicenter of the Buddhist world. Anchored by the 55-meter-high Mahabodhi Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage site constructed originally by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE, the sacred sanctuary houses the diamond throne (Vajrasana) and direct descendant of the legendary Bodhi Tree. Pilgrims and travelers from across the globe gather here amid serene monasteries constructed by Buddhist nations worldwide, including Thailand, Bhutan, Japan, Sri Lanka, and Tibet.
overview.about: A transformative spiritual sanctuary where ancient stupas, butter lamps, chanting monks, and international architecture converge to create one of the most serene sacred landscapes on the planet.

howToReach.roadNote: Conveniently connected via Grand Trunk Road (NH-19) and NH-22 from Gaya, Patna (110 km), and Varanasi (250 km).

topPlaces.name: Mahabodhi Temple Complex (UNESCO Heritage)
topPlaces.description: Iconic 55-meter grand pyramidal temple sanctum marking the spot where Lord Buddha attained enlightenment, housing the gilded statue of Buddha in Bhumisparsha mudra.

image.alt: Mahabodhi Temple Complex (UNESCO Heritage) in Bodh Gaya, Bihar

topPlaces.name: Sacred Bodhi Tree & Vajrasana Throne
topPlaces.description: Venerated fifth-generation descendant of the original Ficus religiosa tree beneath which Buddha sat in meditation, accompanied by Emperor Ashoka’s polished sandstone Diamond Throne.

image.alt: Sacred Bodhi Tree & Vajrasana Throne in Bodh Gaya, Bihar

topPlaces.name: Great Buddha Statue (Daibutsu)
topPlaces.description: Colossal 80-foot red granite and sandstone seated Buddha statue unveiled by the 14th Dalai Lama in 1989, encircled by statues of the ten chief disciples.

image.alt: Great Buddha Statue (Daibutsu) in Bodh Gaya, Bihar

topPlaces.name: Royal Bhutanese Monastery
topPlaces.description: Ornately painted traditional Dzong-style monastery adorned with intricate Himalayan clay reliefs depicting the life and deeds of Gautama Buddha.

image.alt: Royal Bhutanese Monastery in Bodh Gaya, Bihar

topPlaces.name: Wat Thai Bodh Gaya (Royal Thai Temple)
topPlaces.description: Magnificent Thai monastery built in 1957 by King of Thailand, featuring sloping multi-tiered roofs with golden chofas and a massive bronze Buddha image.

image.alt: Wat Thai Bodh Gaya (Royal Thai Temple) in Bodh Gaya, Bihar

topPlaces.name: Dungeshwari Cave Temples (Mahakala Caves)
topPlaces.description: Holy cave hermitage on Pragbodhi Hill where Siddhartha underwent six years of rigorous penance and asceticism before proceeding to the Bodhi Tree.

image.alt: Dungeshwari Cave Temples (Mahakala Caves) in Bodh Gaya, Bihar

topPlaces.name: Metta Buddharam Temple & Butter Lamp Pavilion
topPlaces.description: Modern stainless-steel and white marble Thai temple complex featuring thousands of silver mirrors and evening butter lamp meditation ceremonies.

image.alt: Metta Buddharam Temple & Butter Lamp Pavilion in Bodh Gaya, Bihar

topPlaces.name: Archaeological Society of India Museum Bodh Gaya
topPlaces.description: Historic repository showcasing 1st-century BCE Sunga railings, Yaksha sandstone sculptures, bronze Buddha antiquities, and gold relic caskets.

image.alt: Archaeological Society of India Museum Bodh Gaya in Bodh Gaya, Bihar

itinerary.title: Day 1 — Mahabodhi Enlightenment, Bodhi Tree & International Monasteries

items.note: Witness morning chanting and circumnavigate the ancient stupa complex.
Marvel at the gigantic sandstone statue and Thai architecture.
Examine 2,000-year-old Sunga stone railings and Bhutanese wall frescoes.
Experience thousands of flickering golden butter lamps in temple grounds.

itinerary.title: Day 2 — Dungeshwari Caves & Sujata Kuti Hermitage

items.note: Climb Pragbodhi hill to explore the meditation caves of ascetic Siddhartha.
Visit the earthen stupa dedicated to maiden Sujata across the Falgu river.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit Bodh Gaya?
faq.a: October to March offers cool, pleasant weather (8°C to 24°C), making it ideal for meditation and visiting monasteries.

faq.q: Is photography allowed inside Mahabodhi Temple?
faq.a: Mobile phones are deposited in lockers outside. Cameras are permitted inside with a nominal ticket of ₹100.

faq.q: Can tourists attend chanting sessions at Mahabodhi Temple?
faq.a: Yes, devotees and visitors of all faiths are welcome to sit quietly and join the early morning (5:30 AM) and evening (6:00 PM) chanting sessions.
